summary: Wilhelm Halbfass worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1962–1964) and the University of Göttingen (~1964–1967), later serving as professor at the University of Pennsylvania from 1982 to 2000.
Wilhelm Havers was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at Leipzig (~1915–1917), Bern (~1917–1920), Würzburg (~1920–1929), Breslau (~1929–1937), and Vienna (~1937–1953).

Wilhelm Max Müller worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Berlin (~1883–1885) and Leipzig (~1885–1888) and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1910–1919).

Wilhelm Pertsch worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Berlin (~1850–1854) under Albrecht Weber and Tübingen (~1853–1854) under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as librarian and director at Gotha and Schloss Friedenstein.
Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Schulze (~1906–1911) and Heinrich Lüders (~1909–1911).

Wilhelm Radloff worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin (1854–1858) and Jena (~1858), later directing the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Kunstkamera (1894–1918).

Wilhelm Rau was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig (1940) and Marburg (1946–1949) under Friedrich Weller and Johannes Nobel, and served as Ordinarius at the University of Marburg from 1958 to 1987.
Wilhelm Scherer worked in linguistics. He studied at Vienna and Berlin under Moriz Haupt and Franz Bopp, and held chairs at Vienna (1868–1872), Strasbourg (1872), and Berlin (1877).

Wilhelm Schmidt worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Berlin (~1893–1895) and held posts at the University of Vienna (~1921–1938) and the University of Fribourg (~1939–1951).
Wilhelm Schott specialized in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Berlin (~1823–1826) and later held a post there (~1838–1889).

Wilhelm Schulze worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Berlin and Greifswald under Johannes Schmidt, Heinrich Zimmer, and others, later holding chairs at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Berlin (1902–1932).
Wilhelm Schüler was a Sinologist who held posts at the Seminar for Oriental Languages from ~1904 to 1935, becoming a professor around 1912.

Wilhelm Solf was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Richard Pischel (~1883–1885). He also studied at Jena, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, Kiel, and Göttingen, and held a post at Kiel University (~1887–1888).
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp (~1851–1854) and Moriz Haupt (~1853–1857).

Wilhelm Streitberg worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Münster, Leipzig (under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch), and Berlin, later holding posts at Fribourg (~1889–1898), Münster (1899), Munich (1909), and Leipzig (1898, 1920–1925).

Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh, and served as professor and Ordinarius at the University of Basel (1833; 1835–1869).
Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy. He studied at the universities of Tübingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin between ~1851 and 1856, and held posts at Zurich (1857), Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg (1864).

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen, and Jena under several tutors, founded the University of Berlin (1810), and was a Prussian minister (~1819).
Will B. Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso and studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.
Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge and held a post at the University of Otago (~2005).
